pages.text: In a strong field and the cold, the Hall resistance of a sheet of electrons sits on plateaus at $(thing)h/(νe²)$() - 25 812.807 Ω for ν = 1, exact to a part in a billion, because it counts a topological number. The Laser Cutter cuts $(item)Hall Bar Chips$() from silicon and gold.

A collapsing star keeps its magnetic flux: its field grows as $(thing)(R/r)²$(). A magnetar's is 10¹¹ tesla. Its crust, found in the Accretion Frontier's Pulsar Field, cracks in starquakes; Dirac showed a single magnetic charge would have to be a multiple of h/e.
